anatomy.flutter: Dialog(trigger, content, onOpenChange) wraps OverlayPortal with an OpenTransition; DialogContent lays out DialogHeader/DialogFooter/DialogMedia as bleeding bands via DialogContentGroup (InheritedWidget) around body children in a Column + SingleChildScrollView.
anatomy.web: Dialog > DialogTrigger, DialogPortal > DialogOverlay + DialogPrimitive.Content(data-slot="dialog-content") containing DialogHeader/DialogFooter/DialogMedia/DialogTitle/DialogDescription, exactly the slot list dialog.dart's own header comment cites as "components/ui/dialog.tsx".

api.flutter: DialogContent takes children: List<Widget>, variant: DialogVariant{normal,media}, showCloseButton (default true), onClose; DialogFooter has no showCloseButton param of its own (dialog.dart line 59: "Not ported").
api.web: DialogContent takes showCloseButton (default true) and variant: "default"|"media"; DialogFooter takes an extra showCloseButton (default false) that appends a Button variant="outline" wrapped in DialogClose — the API Reference block documents this as DialogFooter's own prop.
api.note: DialogFooter's showCloseButton is real on the web (dialog.tsx lines 150-171, demoed nowhere in the doc page but present in the component) and explicitly called out in dialog.dart's own "Not ported" section as absent from the Dart DialogFooter — a deliberate, documented omission rather than an oversight, but still a live prop difference between the two APIs.

states.flutter: OverlayPortalState._open drives _content/_overlay AnimationControllers; open() takes primaryFocus into _restoreTo, pushes onto the static _stack, and _takeFocus() calls _scope.nextFocus() on the post-frame callback to land on the first tabbable child (measured: Cancel).
states.web: Docs States block lists rest/closed, hover, focus-visible, pressed (all delegated to the trigger Button), open ("data-open on content and overlay"), disabled trigger, and loading/success/error/empty as N/A with the Note explaining those outcomes belong to alert-dialog's AlertDialogAction instead.

disabled.flutter: DialogContent, DialogHeader and DialogFooter carry no disabled field anywhere in dialog.dart — a dialog is a container, so the only thing that can be disabled is its trigger button, which Button already owns.
disabled.web: The docs States block itself marks disabled as belonging to the trigger ("disabled trigger — Nothing to decide yet") rather than to Dialog, and Dialog/DialogContent/DialogFooter accept no disabled prop in dialog.tsx.
disabled.note: Both sides agree disabled is not a Dialog-level concept: it lives on whatever DialogTrigger wraps (Button), which is audited separately, so n/a applies identically on both sides rather than one side lacking something the other has.

interaction.flutter: _onKey closes on LogicalKeyboardKey.escape unconditionally ("Escape closes every modal on the page ... Drift, reproduced"), while _onPop only closes the topmost entry in the static _stack on Android back/predictive-back, an order with no reference counterpart.
interaction.web: Docs Keyboard block: Enter/Space activates the trigger, Tab/Shift+Tab cycles only inside the dialog, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger; Accessibility block adds "a click on the overlay, and a click outside the content all close the dialog by default."
interaction.note: Escape is transcribed 1:1 (dialog.dart lines 87-94: "Escape follows the reference, back always dismisses"), but the Android back/predictive-back handling in OverlayPortalState._onPop (lines 461-478) is a USER-ORDERED MOBILE ADAPTATION with no web equivalent, since the web has no back-gesture concept — recorded here as expected platform divergence, not compared against the web.

semantics.flutter: OverlayPortalState wraps the panel in Semantics(scopesRoute: true, explicitChildNodes: true) plus a top-level BlockSemantics() so the page behind is unreachable to assistive tech, but sets no namesRoute/label tying the route's accessible name to DialogTitle's text.
semantics.web: Docs Accessibility block: role="dialog" with aria-modal="true", "Accessible name: aria-labelledby, pointed automatically at DialogTitle's generated id ... its absence leaves the dialog unnamed," and "Background inertness: the rest of the page is marked inert."
semantics.note: Web wires an explicit aria-labelledby from the dialog root to DialogTitle's id (Radix's own mechanism); Flutter has no namesRoute/label equivalent and instead relies on explicitChildNodes ordering so a screen reader reads DialogTitle first in sequence — functionally similar (the title is still the first thing announced) but via a different, platform-native semantics mechanism rather than an explicit id relationship, so this is recorded as a platform difference rather than a gap.
